title: Roadblock Check Audit
eyebrow: Proposal · audit of the planned fix (parent issue #587, the roadblock detection fix), nothing built yet

short.lead: I tested the planned roadblock check against real transcripts and found eight weak spots. The fix keeps phrase matching as a cheap first layer. It adds a check of the session record, and an optional second model that judges each reply. You make five choices.
short.hint: Tap a card to see the evidence.
items: I ran test cases through the merged check (tool types, quoting, apostrophes), read how 224 tool results record failure, counted genuine messages (17), scanned 28 real final replies, timed a 5.3 MB transcript, and tried a Stop hook judged by a model. Results are on the eight cards below. Anything I could not measure is labelled as reasoned.

items.caption: Measured items and reasoned items are labelled apart on each card.

items: Three layers instead of one phrase list

Layer 1 is the cheap phrase scan. Layer 2 reads the session record. It wants three failed attempts that each used a different kind of method, such as a file check, a disk search or a package lookup. All three must be about one target, and the reply must list them. Layer 3 is an optional model judge that catches wording no list covers.

items.caption: Each layer covers a gap in the one before it.

items: You approve the audit and your five picks
Your approval is recorded in the decisions log, and the plan page is updated to match.
Pick one option for each question, then tap Copy my reply and paste it into this chat.

changes: chg
1. Claim wording slips past
Curly apostrophes, paraphrases and blockquotes.

Measured: a claim with a curly apostrophe (can’t) was not flagged, and a quoted blockquote line was flagged by mistake. Reasoned: a phrase list never covers every paraphrase, such as "wasn't able to" or "no way to".
Today the pattern needs a straight apostrophe and ignores only quotes and backticks.
Normalise apostrophes, ignore blockquotes and code, and add the optional model judge for paraphrases.
Fewer misses and fewer false alarms.
chg
2. The probe test is too loose
Any command containing ls, where, npm, pip, apt or similar counted.
Measured: a turn that ran git ls-files counted as a probe, so the roadblock claim was accepted without real evidence. This was the main cause on your PC.
Today a probe is any Bash command containing one of 13 program names or command -v.
Count only failed attempts about the target the reply names, and count each kind of method once.
A claim needs real evidence, not a lucky word.
chg
3. Other tools are invisible
PowerShell and MCP tool calls are not recognised.

Measured: after a PowerShell call to Get-Command, the claim was still blocked even though the attempt was real, and the same happened after a failed MCP tool call (a tool from a connected server). Whether your PC uses the PowerShell tool is unverified.
Today only the tool named Bash is read.
Read every tool's result, and add the Windows equivalents of each method class.
No false blocks on Windows or on MCP tools.
chg
4. What counts as failed
Real failures and harmless ones look alike.

Measured in this session: the tool result's error flag (is_error) was set on 9 of 224 results and is reliable. But it is also set by hook refusals and by harmless non-zero exits, such as git commit with nothing to commit. Four results looked like failures but had the flag unset.
Today failure is not read at all.
Failed means is_error, minus hook refusals and a short list of harmless exits, plus results that exited cleanly (code 0) but contain clear failure text.
Evidence rests on real failures.
chg
5. Two escape routes in the plan are weak
A reply that names no target, and a reply that lists fewer than three methods.

Reasoned: counting any three failed results lets unrelated failures satisfy the rule, and "say why" is unchecked. Replacement: the three attempts must share a target word that also appears in the reply or in your request. If the reply lists fewer than three, the model judge checks the reason it gives.
Today the plan allows both, and lists them as known weaknesses.
Attempts must share a target, methods come from a fixed list of kinds, and the model judge checks the reason.
Unrelated failures no longer count.
chg
6. False alarms
Replies that are honest, that quote the rule, that relay a helper's failure, or that really must stop.

Measured: the phrase "next step" appeared in 2 of 28 real final replies, and one of those was a reply discussing the rule itself. Reasoned: a reply relaying a subagent's failure, or needing a licence, login or purchase, is a legitimate stop.
Today every phrase hit blocks up to twice.
A stall phrase flags a reply only if it also hands the decision back to you, a marked exemption covers licence, login, purchase and destructive stops, and the cap of two stays.
Fewer pointless blocks.
chg
7. Which messages start a new turn
Messages that you did not write start a new turn by mistake.

Measured: in this session, 2 of 17 messages counted as yours were automatic system-reminder messages, not you. Each wrongly starts a new turn. That hides earlier attempts and resets the count of blocks so far. Hook feedback is correctly excluded.
Today any message not on a short exclusion list is genuine.
Also exclude system-reminder carriers.
Attempts before the block keep counting.
chg
8. The environment
Mode field, other modes and speed.

Measured: the Stop payload has permission_mode, the whole end-of-turn (Stop) step took 0.8 s on a 5.3 MB transcript, and the check itself adds 0.08 s. Estimate, not measured: 100 MB would take about 15 s. Hook time limits are unknown.
Today a missing mode is not handled and the whole file is read.
If the mode is missing, say so and assume someone is watching. Read only the end of the transcript. Question 5 asks whether the auto and dontAsk modes should count as unattended.
Safe on long sessions.
choices: first
How much checking sits behind the phrase scan?
A
Layers 1 and 2 only: phrase scan plus the record check, no model call
Free and fast, but wording no list covers still slips through.
B
Add layer 3: a model-judged Stop hook on every turn end (my suggestion)
Measured once: the judge flagged the claim, gave an actionable reason, and passed after methods were listed. Its call cost $0.004 for two evaluations, against $0.244 for the main model in that run.
C
Add layer 3 as an agent hook that reads the transcript itself
Strongest, since it can verify each listed method really ran, but it is slower and costs more. Not tested.
B closes the wording gap for a tiny measured cost. One run is a small sample, so the cost is an estimate.
second
How is a different method decided?
A
A closed table of method classes: existence check, disk search, package database, run it, ask the environment, other tool (my suggestion)
Three attempts must fall in three different kinds, so which, where and command -v together count as one attempt (all are existence checks).
B
A different command program or tool name
Simpler, but three existence checks would count as three methods.
A stops the cheapest way of gaming the rule.
third
What about stops that are really yours to settle?
A
The reply marks NEEDS YOU for a licence, login, purchase or destructive step, and is exempt from the three-attempt rule (my suggestion)
Matches the rule that those four stay yours. In unattended mode the agent carries on with other work.
B
No exemption: the cap of two handles it
Simplest, but the agent is told to try again at things it can never do.
A keeps the block for real roadblocks only.
fourth
When does a stall phrase such as "next step" flag a reply?
A
Only with hand-back wording too: ends in a question, or says your call, let me know, or waiting for you (my suggestion)
Removes the 2 false flags in 28 real replies, which came from ordinary "next step" lines.
B
On the phrase alone, as you approved in your 2026-11-23 answers
Catches more, but flags ordinary replies in unattended runs.
A still catches the reply from the Castle session on your PC, which ended with "Your call".
fifth
Which permission modes should count as unattended, with no one watching?
A
Unattended runs and bypassPermissions only, as you answered on 2026-11-23 (my suggestion)
Matches what you said, word for word.
B
Also auto and dontAsk
Those modes also run without a person confirming each step, but you did not name them.
A keeps to your answer. B is one line to add later.

wrapup.summary: This audit found eight weak spots in the planned check and proposes three layers: phrases, a record check of three related failed attempts, and an optional model judge.
wrapup.changing: The claim pattern, the evidence test, the failure rule, the window rule and the plan page for issues #588 (detection), #589 (the three-attempt rule) and #590 (never waiting).
